messages:
maria-l: paging oncall — production alert: KV cache reuse appears to be leaking state between requests when continuous batching is enabled. some customers seeing incorrect tokens in completions and persistent stale values. spike in user-facing errors and tail latency. incident bot kicked off.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1901203456 | Severity: P1 | Started by: maria-l
kevin-w: I'm on it. quick question: is this limited to the new batching rollouts from last night? saw a config change to max_batch_wait_ms -> 12ms.
devon: yes, the rollout to dedicated-gpu-pool-7 included continuous batching + kv-reuse opt. I see increased "stale_kv_detected" logs on that pool.
sre-jun: tracing one trace: request A writes kv key kX at seq_offset 1024, but subsequent request B read kX with seq_offset 512 and reused value. looks like reuse logic didn't validate seq_offset monotonicity.
oncall-mike: customer impact: CS reported 3 customers with incorrect completions (sensitive prompt echo), two have alerting SLAs. listing: cust-zenith, cust-lumen, cust-mira. CS @amy-cs is on call with them.
amy-cs: I'm on calls with cust-zenith, they see repeated old completions for multi-turn chat sessions. they're upset, flagged as degraded. pushing status page update now. :frowning:
kevin-w: ok immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable KV reuse feature flag globally 2) rollback continuous batching rollout to previous stable config (min_batch=1/disable convergence) 3) restart worker pool on dedicated-gpu-pool-7 with cleared caches 4) run canary traffic. executing step 1 now.
deploy-bot: Feature flag toggled: kv_cache_reuse -> OFF by kevin-w (prod).
sre-jun: toggled. seeing drop in 'stale_kv' counts but latency increased slightly from batching rollback. still better than incorrect outputs.
devon: applying hotfix to batching config: set max_batch_wait_ms back to 1ms and disable adaptive batch merging. posting config snippet:

```
# release-hotfix
continuous_batching:
  enabled: false
  max_batch_wait_ms: 1
  min_batch_size: 1
```
ops-bot: Rolling restart initiated for dedicated-gpu-pool-7 (3 nodes) — restart sequence started by devops.
oncall-mike: handoff: I'm leaving at 15:30 UTC, @sre-jun will take primary. leaving notes: keep kv_reuse OFF, watch for errors>0.5% and any stale_kv logs.
sre-jun: acknowledged. running full smoke across model queue. running targeted test to reproduce: multi-turn with page sizes and purposely misaligned seq offsets.
kevin-w: found quick repro locally: run two in-flight requests with different seq offsets and shared cache shard -> reuse happens when cache insertion didn't set seq_offset metadata. patch ready that enforces seq_offset equality and clears entry if mismatch.
devon: can we push patch as a canary? patch changes:

```
# kv cache change
on cache_get(key):
  if entry.seq_offset != request.seq_offset:
    return MISS
```
```
# also add per-request cache clear on session_reset
```

deploy-bot: Canary deploy of kv-fix (rev abc7d9) to 1 node in dedicated-gpu-pool-7.
sre-jun: canary metrics look good — no stale_kv logs, no regression in token throughput. moving to 20% traffic.
kevin-w: after 30m of canary, metrics stable. plan: full rollout in 10m, then re-enable controlled batching if safe.
amy-cs: cust-zenith reports their chats look correct now. they'll keep monitoring. sending praise for the quick response.
ops-bot: Full rollout complete: kv-fix rev abc7d9 deployed to pool-7. kv_cache_reuse remains OFF until postmortem.
maria-l: customer impact summary for incident channel: 3 customers affected, degraded for ~45m, incorrect completions observed for multi-turn sessions due to KV reuse with stale seq offsets. mitigations: feature flag off, batching rollback, cache-clearing restarts, canary + full rollout of seq_offset check patch. no data exfiltration detected.
kevin-w: postmortem action items I will own: 1) add unit + integration tests for seq_offset validation in cache layer 2) add alert for 'stale_kv_detected' threshold 3) implement safer default: cache entries include insertion-id and TTL tied to request boundary 4) add runbook steps for quick disable and restart.
devon: ops items: create a one-click rollback in console for batching config and feature flag in emergencies. also add a smoke test in deploy pipeline to run multi-turn chat sequences.
oncall-mike: thanks team. I'll file an interim RCA doc and schedule the full postmortem tomorrow. tag: follow-up owners: kevin-w (kernel fixes), devon (deploy/runbook), amy-cs (customer comms).
amy-cs: sent follow-up emails and status updates to affected customers; offering deeper postmortem meeting.
maria-l: incident declared resolved at 1901203899 — services stable, no ongoing incorrect completions. leaving incident open for postmortem until fixes merged and tested. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1901203456 status -> RESOLVED (mitigated) by kevin-w
sre-jun: note for postmortem: root cause hypothesis — reuse logic assumed monotonic seq_offsets across batched request merges; paging semantics sometimes surface older seq offsets when merging KV snapshots across partial pages. fix included stricter seq_offset equality and explicit per-request cache boundaries.
kevin-w: PR #4829 created with tests and changelog, targeting next deploy window. assigning reviewers: @devon, @sre-jun. closing notes: avoid re-enabling kv_cache_reuse until thorough testing with paged KV workloads.
maria-l: great work — quick and calm. we'll do a blameless postmortem.
